Change c0480. Location: 1818 Vol. III, Ch. VII; 1831 Ch. XXIV.

Context before (unchanged): It rung on my ears long and heavily; the mountains re-echoed it, and I felt as if all hell surrounded me with mockery and laughter.

1818 text: Surely in that moment I should have been possessed by phrenzy, and have destroyed my miserable existence, but that my vow was heard, and that I was reserved for vengeance. The laughter died away: when a well-known and abhorred voice, apparently close to my ear, addressed me in an audible whisper—"I am satisfied: miserable wretch! you have determined to live, and I am satisfied."

1831 text: Surely in that moment I should have been possessed by frenzy, and have destroyed my miserable existence, but that my vow was heard, and that I was reserved for vengeance. The laughter died away; when a well-known and abhorred voice, apparently close to my ear, addressed me in an audible whisper—"I am satisfied: miserable wretch! you have determined to live, and I am satisfied."

Diff: Surely in that moment I should have been possessed by [-phrenzy-] {+frenzy+} , and have destroyed my miserable existence, but that my vow was heard, and that I was reserved for vengeance. The laughter died away [-:-] {+;+} when a well-known and abhorred voice, apparently close to my ear, addressed me in an audible whisper—" I am satisfied: miserable wretch! you have determined to live, and I am satisfied. "

Context after (unchanged): I darted towards the spot from which the sound proceeded; but the devil eluded my grasp.

result.rationale: Main change is orthographic: 'phrenzy' becomes 'frenzy'. The colon-to-semicolon swap after 'died away' is punctuation only, with no change in wording or meaning.
